app.name: Treatable
app.purpose: Treatable helps you find public clinical studies and prepare questions to ask a study team.
disclaimer.matchingLimits: Matching does not establish eligibility, safety, or benefit.
disclaimer.scoreMeaning: A match score is not a probability of eligibility, enrollment, or treatment benefit.
disclaimer.distance: Distance preferences are not medical exclusions.
disclaimer.unknownEligibility: Eligibility information that is not known stays marked unknown. Only the study team can confirm eligibility.
disclaimer.participationDraftOnly: Participation help is limited to drafts that you review. Treatable does not submit applications, email researchers, enroll you in a study, complete clinical screening, or sign consent for you.
disclaimer.publicRecords: Study records come from the public ClinicalTrials.gov registry and can be out of date. Confirm recruitment status, eligibility, and locations with the study team.
disclaimer.aiOutput: Comparisons and questions written by OpenAI can be wrong or incomplete. Check them against the source record and ask the study team.
disclaimer.notClinicallyValidated: Treatable has not been clinically validated. It does not diagnose conditions or recommend treatment.
disclaimer.notAnonymous: Minimized health information is not anonymous.
disclaimer.notPhiReady: Not PHI-ready. PHI means protected health information. A business associate agreement (BAA) is a contract about how a service provider handles that information. Treatable has not confirmed whether a BAA or data retention terms cover your OpenAI account, and it does not verify a BAA.
disclaimer.noComplianceClaim: Treatable makes no claim of HIPAA compliance or legal sufficiency.
operator.label: Operator
operator.name: Kurt Lehnardt - Developer of Treatable
operator.noticeOnly: The operator and privacy contact are shown for your information only. They are never sent to a model.
operator.noRecordLookup: Requests to OpenAI run under your own OpenAI account. The operator has no access to that account and cannot look up or delete OpenAI records for you.
disclosure.ctgov.heading: What ClinicalTrials.gov receives
disclosure.ctgov.body: The words you type to search, including any symptoms, are sent to clinicaltrials.gov over HTTPS as part of the web address (URL) of the request, together with the country (United States) and at most a US state. Do not type names or other identifying details. ClinicalTrials.gov's own policies apply to that request. The request does not include your ZIP code or coordinates, and Treatable calculates distance itself inside the app.
disclosure.ctgov.networkNote: Like any web request, it also reveals your network address to the service.
disclosure.openai.heading: What OpenAI receives
disclosure.openai.body: Only after you confirm: a condition term you selected from public ClinicalTrials.gov vocabulary, your age band, your US state if you chose to share it, your sex if you chose to share it, and public study fields from ClinicalTrials.gov records.
disclosure.openai.conditionTerm: The condition term comes from public ClinicalTrials.gov vocabulary, such as condition and MeSH terms on returned study records. It is never text that you typed.
disclosure.openai.account: OpenAI receives these requests under your own OpenAI API key, so OpenAI can link them to your OpenAI account. OpenAI also sees your network address.
disclosure.openai.neverSent: The request content never includes free-text symptoms or notes, ZIP codes, coordinates, exact age, date of birth, your name, or your contact details.
disclosure.openai.studyContacts: Study contact details are shown to you in the app but are never sent to OpenAI.
disclosure.separation: ClinicalTrials.gov and OpenAI receive different information. Searching does not send anything to OpenAI.
disclosure.agentsRetention: The OpenAI Agents API retains session state until the session is deleted. It is not compatible with Zero Data Retention, an OpenAI option for eligible customers that limits how long API data is kept. After an analysis, Treatable attempts to cancel any running work and delete the session, and it reports any failure. OpenAI states that deletion removes the session from the API and that physical cleanup may continue afterwards. Treatable does not promise instant physical erasure.
disclosure.agentsTracing: OpenAI turns on tracing by default for new Agents sessions. A trace records the inputs, outputs, and tool results of the session and is shown in the OpenAI dashboard under Logs, Agents, for the project that owns your API key. Anyone who can open that project's logs may be able to see it. OpenAI documents no per-session setting to turn tracing off, and its documentation does not say whether deleting a session also removes its trace.
disclosure.agentsInterrupted: If Treatable is closed or the device loses power during an operation, cleanup may not run, and the Agents session can remain in your OpenAI project until it is deleted.
disclosure.decisionsRetention: Relevance scoring uses the OpenAI Decisions API. OpenAI's data controls page lists no stored application state for this endpoint other than prompt caching, which OpenAI says expires after 24 hours.
disclosure.abuseMonitoring: OpenAI states that abuse-monitoring logs, which can include request content, are kept for up to 30 days by default for Decisions and Agents requests unless longer retention is required by law. OpenAI's documentation does not say that deleting an Agents session removes these logs.
disclosure.noTraining: OpenAI states that API data is not used to train or improve its models unless the owner of the OpenAI account has opted in to share data with OpenAI. With your own API key, that choice is made in your own OpenAI account.
disclosure.cannotRetract: Ending a session cannot take back data that was already sent to ClinicalTrials.gov or OpenAI.
disclosure.credentials: OpenAI features use your own OpenAI API key, which Treatable keeps only in storage that uses your operating system's credential system. There is no plaintext fallback. Without a saved key, OpenAI features stay locked.
disclosure.limits: If your device has malware, or someone has administrator access to it, Treatable cannot protect your information. Treatable also cannot protect against a compromised operating system, privileged debuggers, or memory forensics.
notice.title: Privacy and health-data notice
notice.regionLabel: Privacy and health-data notice. Scroll to the end to continue.
notice.scrollHint: Scroll to the end of this notice to enable the acknowledgment.
notice.acknowledgmentLabel: I have read this notice and I understand the health-data disclosure and the provider retention described above.
notice.acknowledgmentSessionOnly: This acknowledgment lasts only for the current session and is not saved.
notice.section.01.heading: Your choice
notice.section.01.body: Searching ClinicalTrials.gov and screening results inside the app work without OpenAI. OpenAI analysis is optional. It starts only after you read this notice, acknowledge it, review the exact request that would be sent, and confirm sending as a separate step. If you decline, you can keep searching and screening.
notice.section.02.heading: What ClinicalTrials.gov receives
notice.section.02.body: The words you type to search, including any symptoms, are sent to clinicaltrials.gov over HTTPS as part of the web address (URL) of the request, together with the country (United States) and at most a US state. Do not type names or other identifying details. ClinicalTrials.gov's own policies apply to that request. The request does not include your ZIP code or coordinates, and Treatable calculates distance itself inside the app. Like any web request, it also reveals your network address to the service. Searching does not send anything to OpenAI.
notice.section.03.heading: What OpenAI receives
notice.section.03.body: Only after you confirm: a condition term you selected from public ClinicalTrials.gov vocabulary, your age band, your US state if you chose to share it, your sex if you chose to share it, and public study fields from ClinicalTrials.gov records. The condition term comes from public ClinicalTrials.gov vocabulary, such as condition and MeSH terms on returned study records. It is never text that you typed. OpenAI receives these requests under your own OpenAI API key, so OpenAI can link them to your OpenAI account. OpenAI also sees your network address. The request content never includes free-text symptoms or notes, ZIP codes, coordinates, exact age, date of birth, your name, or your contact details. Study contact details are shown to you in the app but are never sent to OpenAI.
notice.section.04.heading: Minimized is not anonymous
notice.section.04.body: A condition term, an age band, and a US state can still identify a person when they are combined. Minimized health information is not anonymous. Not PHI-ready. PHI means protected health information. A business associate agreement (BAA) is a contract about how a service provider handles that information. Treatable has not confirmed whether a BAA or data retention terms cover your OpenAI account, and it does not verify a BAA. Treatable makes no claim of HIPAA compliance or legal sufficiency.
notice.section.05.heading: OpenAI Agents retention
notice.section.05.body: The OpenAI Agents API retains session state until the session is deleted. It is not compatible with Zero Data Retention, an OpenAI option for eligible customers that limits how long API data is kept. After an analysis, Treatable attempts to cancel any running work and delete the session, and it reports any failure. OpenAI states that deletion removes the session from the API and that physical cleanup may continue afterwards. Treatable does not promise instant physical erasure. OpenAI turns on tracing by default for new Agents sessions. A trace records the inputs, outputs, and tool results of the session and is shown in the OpenAI dashboard under Logs, Agents, for the project that owns your API key. Anyone who can open that project's logs may be able to see it. OpenAI documents no per-session setting to turn tracing off, and its documentation does not say whether deleting a session also removes its trace. If Treatable is closed or the device loses power during an operation, cleanup may not run, and the Agents session can remain in your OpenAI project until it is deleted. Ending a session cannot take back data that was already sent to ClinicalTrials.gov or OpenAI.
notice.section.06.heading: OpenAI Decisions retention, logs, and training
notice.section.06.body: Relevance scoring uses the OpenAI Decisions API. OpenAI's data controls page lists no stored application state for this endpoint other than prompt caching, which OpenAI says expires after 24 hours. OpenAI states that abuse-monitoring logs, which can include request content, are kept for up to 30 days by default for Decisions and Agents requests unless longer retention is required by law. OpenAI's documentation does not say that deleting an Agents session removes these logs. OpenAI states that API data is not used to train or improve its models unless the owner of the OpenAI account has opted in to share data with OpenAI. With your own API key, that choice is made in your own OpenAI account.
notice.section.07.heading: Your OpenAI API key
notice.section.07.body: OpenAI features use your own OpenAI API key, which Treatable keeps only in storage that uses your operating system's credential system. There is no plaintext fallback. Without a saved key, OpenAI features stay locked. Treatable asks for your key only on the key screen and contains no shared OpenAI key.
notice.section.08.heading: Session-only handling
notice.section.08.body: Treatable has no saved profiles, notes, search history, analytics, or crash reporting. Your entries, results, request previews, and trace exist only in memory during the current session. Ending the session removes them from the app and cancels work in progress. Any cache of public study records is kept separate from your entries, is labeled as public study data, and shows when each record was retrieved.
notice.section.09.heading: Limits of these controls
notice.section.09.body: If your device has malware, or someone has administrator access to it, Treatable cannot protect your information. Treatable also cannot protect against a compromised operating system, privileged debuggers, or memory forensics. Data held in system memory, crash dumps, or files outside the control of the app can remain after a session ends.
notice.section.10.heading: Before anything is sent
notice.section.10.body: Before anything is sent to OpenAI, you review the exact request bodies and public tool results in a preview, and then you confirm sending as a separate step. A prepared request expires after five minutes. Decisions and Agents can each be sent once from it. Changing any entry discards the preview and your confirmation. Stopping a request asks for cancellation and cleanup, but Treatable cannot promise that OpenAI has erased the data.
notice.section.11.heading: What results mean
notice.section.11.body: Research information, not medical advice. A match score is not a probability of eligibility, enrollment, or treatment benefit. Distance preferences are not medical exclusions. Eligibility information that is not known stays marked unknown. Only the study team can confirm eligibility. Comparisons and questions written by OpenAI can be wrong or incomplete. Check them against the source record and ask the study team. Participation help is limited to drafts that you review. Treatable does not submit applications, email researchers, enroll you in a study, complete clinical screening, or sign consent for you.
notice.section.12.heading: Operator and privacy contact
notice.section.12.body: Operator: Kurt Lehnardt - Developer of Treatable. Privacy contact: privacy.6vpc5@mailer.me. The operator and privacy contact are shown for your information only. They are never sent to a model. Requests to OpenAI run under your own OpenAI account. The operator has no access to that account and cannot look up or delete OpenAI records for you.
consent.separateConfirmationNote: Acknowledging the notice does not send anything. Sending needs a separate confirmation of the exact request.
consent.prepareButton: Prepare exact request preview (no OpenAI call)
consent.previewExplanation: This preview shows the complete request bodies and the public tool results that would be sent to OpenAI. It contains the health information you selected. Preparing a preview does not contact OpenAI.
consent.previewNoCredentials: Your API key is not part of the preview and is never shown.
consent.expiryNote: A prepared request expires after five minutes. Decisions and Agents can each be sent once from it.
consent.invalidationNote: Changing any entry discards the preview and your confirmation.
consent.confirmLabel: I reviewed this exact request and I confirm sending it to OpenAI for the operation I choose below.
payload.heading: What you choose to share with OpenAI
payload.notSharedNote: Free-text symptoms and notes, ZIP code, coordinates, exact age, date of birth, names, and contact details are not part of this request.
credential.heading: Your OpenAI API key
credential.explanation: Treatable uses your own OpenAI API key. It keeps the key only in storage that uses your operating system's credential system.
credential.lockedWithoutKey: OpenAI features stay locked until a saved key is available.
credential.prompt: Enter your OpenAI API key. Treatable keeps it only in storage that uses your operating system's credential system.
credential.neverInChat: Never share your key in chat or in a message.
credential.noSharedKey: Treatable contains no shared OpenAI key.
credential.removeConfirm: Remove your saved OpenAI API key? OpenAI features will be locked until you save a key again.
credential.statusLocked: Your operating system's credential system is locked or unavailable.
credential.keepsAfterSession: Ending a session does not remove your saved key.
error.networkOffline: You appear to be offline. Search and OpenAI analysis need a network connection. Anything already on screen is kept.
error.ctgovUnavailable: ClinicalTrials.gov did not respond or is unavailable. Try again in a moment.
error.ctgovRateLimited: ClinicalTrials.gov is limiting requests right now. Wait a moment, then try again.
error.openaiUnavailable: OpenAI is unavailable or returned an error. Your local results are kept. Check the trace to see what was sent and whether cleanup finished.
error.consentRequired: Acknowledge the notice, review the exact request preview, and confirm sending before anything is sent to OpenAI.
error.consentExpired: The prepared request expired after five minutes. Prepare a new preview and confirm it again.
error.consentInvalidated: You changed an entry, so the preview and your confirmation were discarded. Prepare a new preview and confirm it again.
error.consentUsed: This operation was already sent from this prepared request. Prepare a new preview to send it again.
error.credentialMissing: No OpenAI API key is saved. OpenAI features stay locked. Save your key to continue.
error.credentialLocked: Your operating system's credential system is locked or unavailable. OpenAI features stay locked. Unlock it and try again.
error.cancelled: Cancelled. Cleanup of any OpenAI session was attempted. Check the trace for the result. Your local results are kept.
error.deletionFailed: Deletion of the OpenAI session failed or could not be confirmed. Provider data may remain. Requests to OpenAI run under your own OpenAI account. The operator has no access to that account and cannot look up or delete OpenAI records for you.
error.deletionNotAttempted: The OpenAI session could not be identified, so deletion could not be attempted. Provider data may remain.
error.requestTooLarge: The request is larger than the allowed size and was not sent. Choose fewer items and prepare the preview again.
error.invalidInput: Some entries are not valid. Check the entries and try again.
error.preparationFailed: Preparation failed. Nothing was sent to OpenAI.
error.analysisIncomplete: The analysis did not complete. Provider data may remain. Check the cleanup status in the trace. Your local results are kept.
error.componentUnavailable: Treatable's search and analysis component is not responding. End the session and start a new one.
error.unknown: Something went wrong. Your local results are kept.
trace.heading: Session-only trace
trace.explanation: This trace exists only in memory during the current session. It is never saved as history. Ending the session clears it, but that cannot take back data that was already sent.
trace.mode.mockedNote: Mocked: a test adapter produced this result and no request reached OpenAI.
trace.mode.liveNote: Live: this result comes from a response from the OpenAI API that passed Treatable's format checks.
trace.cleanupStatus.deleted: Deletion acknowledged by OpenAI. Physical removal can happen later.
trace.cleanupStatus.failed: Deletion failed. Provider data may remain.
trace.cleanupStatus.unconfirmed: Deletion could not be attempted or confirmed.
session.endDescription: Ending the session removes your entries, results, request previews, and trace from the app, cancels work in progress, and requests deletion of any OpenAI session.
session.endCleared: Removed from the app: your entries, the notice acknowledgment, prepared requests and confirmations, results, and the trace.
session.endNotCleared: Not removed: data already sent to ClinicalTrials.gov or OpenAI, your saved API key, and anything outside the control of the app, such as system memory or crash dumps.
session.endDone: Session ended. Your entries and results were cleared.
session.nothingSaved: Nothing you enter is saved. Treatable has no saved profiles, notes, or history.
cache.label: Public study data cache
cache.description: This cache is kept separate from anything you enter. It holds only public ClinicalTrials.gov study records, and each record shows when it was retrieved.
cache.staleWarning: Cached public study data can be out of date. Check the source record on ClinicalTrials.gov.
